title: Structural quality gate catches table/code-block loss

brief.why: Trafilatura passes the 10% ratio check but drops critical structured content. ISO country codes page: 249-row data table stripped despite include_tables=True (trafilatura output 96% of page text but zero table data). Python docs: code blocks flattened into inline text. The ratio check measures quantity not quality — structural degradation is invisible.
brief.what: 1. After trafilatura extraction, count structural markers in the output (pipe-tables or markdown tables, fenced code blocks) 2. Compare against page DOM signals via eval: number of <table> rows with >2 cells, number of <pre> or <code> blocks with >50 chars 3. If page has significant tables/code but trafilatura output has none, fall through to Readability which preserves both better 4. Thresholds: page has >=5 table data rows and output has 0 table markers → reject. Page has >=2 long code blocks and output has 0 fenced blocks → reject 5. Add tests for both table-loss and code-loss detection 6. Smoke test against ISO country codes page and Python asyncio docs
brief.done: ISO country codes page produces output containing table data (country names and codes). Python asyncio docs produce output with fenced code blocks. Cascade falls through to Readability when trafilatura drops structure. Existing pages (Wikipedia article, ONS, HN) unaffected.

title: React controlled inputs defeat type — document nativeInputValueSetter pattern

brief.why: type dispatches CDP key events which React controlled components ignore. Discovered on myitv search SPA. The workaround (nativeInputValueSetter + dispatchEvent) is in CLAUDE.md but could be a built-in verb or auto-detection.
brief.what: 1. Consider a type-react verb or auto-fallback in type when value doesn't change 2. At minimum, add to passe skill as a documented pattern 3. Test against common React frameworks (Next.js, CRA, Vite)
brief.done: Either type handles React inputs automatically or the workaround is documented in both CLAUDE.md and the passe skill

title: Test trafilatura install path with lxml on clean machine

brief.why: Trafilatura pulls 17 packages including lxml (needs C compilation). Passe currently has only websockets. Need to verify uv tool install works cleanly on macOS and Linux without surprises.
brief.what: 1. Test uv tool install passe on a clean sprite/sandbox 2. Verify lxml builds without system deps 3. Check total install size and time 4. Consider whether lxml wheels are available for all targets
brief.done: uv tool install passe works on both macOS and Linux with trafilatura included, no manual intervention needed

title: Event buffer doesn't grow unbounded in long scripts

brief.why: CDPClient.event_buffer stores every CDP event that fires with no waiter. Long scripts that don't use wait-navigation accumulate Page.loadEventFired, Page.frameNavigated etc. Not a memory bomb (small dicts) but unbounded growth is untidy.
brief.what: 1. Add a max buffer size (e.g. 100 events) or TTL-based eviction 2. Consider only buffering navigation-related events since that's the primary use case 3. Test with a long script (50+ steps) to verify buffer doesn't grow
brief.done: Event buffer has a documented bound. Long scripts don't accumulate stale events.

brief.why: Ratio warning unit tests use mocks — need a real browser test to prove the warning fires on actual client-rendered content
brief.what: 1. Create minimal SPA fixture (HTML+JS that renders content client-side) where Readability extracts poorly 2. Write pytest integration test that serves fixture, runs passe read, asserts warning fires 3. Mark test so it only runs when Chrome is available
brief.done: pytest test hits ratio warning path with real browser and real Readability extraction

title: read verb extracts cleanly from any page, not just articles

brief.why: read uses Readability.js which only works on articles. SPAs, intranet pages, noisy sites all fail. Trafilatura is better but runs Python-side. Combining Chrome's rendered DOM with trafilatura gives clean extraction from any authenticated page — a capability no single tool has today.
brief.what: 1. Add trafilatura dependency to pyproject.toml 2. Refactor do_read to get outerHTML from Chrome then run trafilatura Python-side 3. Keep Readability.js as fallback when trafilatura returns nothing 4. Keep innerText as last-resort fallback 5. Preserve the ratio warning system against trafilatura output 6. Update tests 7. Update CLAUDE.md
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto https://my.itv.com/some-page; read /tmp/out.md' produces clean markdown via trafilatura. Fallback chain works: trafilatura → Readability → innerText. Ratio warnings still fire. All tests pass.

brief.done: Bug fixed, three new tests pass, full suite green

brief.why: The flattener is a module-level JS constant in cli.py wedged between do_snapshot and do_read. Readability and Turndown JS live in _libs.py. A future Claude reading the code will wonder why the placement differs. Answer: flattener is our code, libs are third-party — but that's not documented.
brief.what: 1. Move SHADOW_FLATTEN_JS to _libs.py 2. Add a comment in _libs.py explaining the distinction (our code vs bundled third-party) 3. Import and use from cli.py 4. Verify tests pass
brief.done: _libs.py contains all JS constants. Comment explains the organization. Tests pass.

title: Passe doesn't lose fast navigations to a race condition

brief.why: wait-navigation registers its Page.loadEventFired listener AFTER the triggering action (click, press) has already dispatched. Fast navigations fire the event before the waiter exists, so it's dropped and wait-navigation hangs until timeout.
brief.what: 1. Add event buffering to CDPClient — store events that fire with no waiter 2. Check buffer in wait_for_event before registering a new future 3. Test: click that triggers navigation followed by wait-navigation resolves instantly
brief.done: Script 'click .nav-link; wait-navigation' resolves without timeout when the click triggers a fast navigation. Existing do_navigate (listener-before-dispatch) still works. Existing tests pass.

title: Fix -c inline parsing to preserve JS semicolons

brief.why: replace(';', newline) destroys semicolons inside eval/assert JS expressions
brief.what: 1. Read cmd_run and parse_script to understand the current flow 2. Design delimiter strategy — '; ' (semicolon-space) as DSL separator since JS semicolons in expressions won't have trailing space before next verb 3. Update cmd_run inline parsing 4. Update existing regression test and add positive test 5. Update CLAUDE.md footgun note
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto URL; eval "var x = 1; x"' works — eval gets the full expression

title: Bundled JS in _libs.py is minified

brief.why: The bundled Readability.js and Turndown.js in _libs.py are 117KB unminified. They're injected into Chrome via Runtime.evaluate on every read call — smaller payloads mean faster injection.

brief.done: _libs.py is under 50KB. passe run -c 'goto URL; read' produces identical output to before. Build script is reusable for future lib updates.

title: Log warning when trafilatura import or extract fails silently

brief.why: The except Exception: pass in do_read silently swallows trafilatura failures. If trafilatura breaks in a point release, read would silently fall back to Readability and nobody would know. The source field in output helps, but a stderr warning on failure would make the silent fallback visible.
brief.what: 1. In the trafilatura try/except block, catch the exception and log it to stderr as [read] trafilatura failed: {error}, falling back to Readability 2. Distinguish import errors (missing dep) from extraction errors (bad HTML) in the message 3. Add a test that verifies the warning appears on trafilatura failure
brief.done: When trafilatura.extract raises, stderr shows a warning with the error message. Test confirms warning is emitted.

title: Passe warns when read extraction looks incomplete

brief.why: read reports ok:true even when Readability captures garbage (cookie banners, animated content, SPA nav chrome). No signal to the caller that extraction is incomplete — discovered through field testing against Daily Mail, entire.io, etc.
brief.what: 1. Modify EXTRACT_JS to return pageTextLength (document.body.innerText.length) alongside markdown 2. In do_read, compare extracted markdown length vs page text length — warn if <10% 3. Add warning field to step info in run_script for read verb 4. Warn on fallback extraction too
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto SPA-page; read' emits a warning in stderr NDJSON when extraction is <10% of page text. Fallback extractions also warn. Warning visible in step_info but does not set ok:false (it's a warning, not an error).

title: outerHTML includes shadow DOM content — extractors see the full page

brief.why: document.documentElement.outerHTML skips shadow root content. MDN uses <mdn-code-example> web components with code inside shadow DOM — 17 code examples (8KB) invisible to both trafilatura and Readability. Any site using web components loses content silently.
brief.what: 1. Write a JS flattener function that walks the DOM tree, finds elements with .shadowRoot, and inlines shadow root children into the light DOM before serialization 2. Replace the do_eval('document.documentElement.outerHTML') call in do_read with the flattener 3. Test against MDN Promise page — should recover all 17 code examples (8191 chars) 4. Test against regular pages (Wikipedia, ONS) — flattener must not break non-shadow-DOM pages 5. Test performance — flattening adds DOM walking overhead, measure on a heavy page
brief.done: passe run -c 'goto MDN_PROMISE_URL; read /tmp/out.md' produces markdown with fenced code blocks from shadow DOM. grep -c backtick-fence returns >0. Regular pages unaffected. No performance regression >100ms.
